unlisted_practices: Deploy privacy-preserving technologies such as federated learning and differential privacy that minimize data exposure while enabling inter-institutional learning.
Require transparency and explainability of AI systems to support accountability.
Strengthen legal protections against re-identification and discriminatory misuse of health data.
Establish equitable benefit-sharing mechanisms in commercial partnerships involving patient data.
Explicitly recognize relational and familial privacy so that one patient's consent does not automatically override the privacy interests of relatives.
Limit secondary use of patient data for AI development.

screen.reason: Narrative ethical and policy analysis discussing privacy, ethics, and governance challenges of AI in precision oncology, offering recommendations for multi-layered governance.
